status: DRAFT: frozen only on Madhav's approval; nothing is built or recorded before it
title: SF1: does a stock's strength flip when the market is falling? (forward shadow, Nifty 500, India only)
why: SP3 scored its situation features one at a time (ridge, main effects only), and almost every fit chose the heaviest shrinkage: the features added little alone. A descriptive look on SP3's development years 2010-2017 (15 Nov 2026) asked whether COMBINATIONS carry what main effects cannot see. Across all 210 feature pairs nothing passed a strict bar, but one story repeated in both halves (2010-13, 2014-17) and at both 20 and 60 sessions: with the Nifty below its 50- and 200-day averages, stocks that look strong (0-20% above their own 50-day, a high 20-session return, RETEST setups) did worse than random liquid stocks bought the same day, and beaten-down stocks did better; with the Nifty above both, beaten-down stocks kept lagging. It rests on about 13 falling spells of 10+ sessions, its month-level t values sit between 1.2 and 1.9, and it was picked after looking, so it is a lead, not a finding. It matters now because the managed book's replacements must be above both their own averages and within 8% of the 50-day, ranked by strength against the Nifty 500: in a falling market that is exactly the bucket the look flagged.

origin.look: ~/ananta_runs/sp3_interaction_look/ (look.py, detail.py, absolute.py; look_hold_20d_nostop.json, look_hold_60d_nostop.json, cells_*.csv). Dev years 2010-2017 only; SP3 validation 2018-2023 and every sealed year untouched
origin.counted: every variant tried is counted: 210 pairs x 2 exits (420 pair looks, 846 cells each) in the look; this registration is the one hypothesis taken forward from them
origin.look_numbers_20d: bps over 20 sessions vs same-day random stocks, 2010-13 / 2014-17: falling market and 0-20% above own 50-day: main effects expected +125 / +74, got ~0 / -35; falling market and high 20-session return: -138 / -165 vs expected; falling market and below own 50-day: +50 / +84 vs random; rising market and below own 50-day: -160 / -84 vs random

definitions.regime: Nifty 50's close on the evening of recording against its own 50- and 200-day averages (the same rule as SP3's nifty_trend): FALLING = below both, RISING = above both, MIXED = otherwise. Read through india/sealed.read_index purpose paper_context, as the paper engine already does
definitions.universe: every symbol on NSE's newest Nifty 500 list with at least 210 daily bars, close at least the managed book's min_price_inr and 60-day median turnover at least its min_turnover_cr (india/paper_config.json, books.managed), from the same adjusted bars the managed book reads (india/managed.bars)
definitions.strong: close above its own 50-day average by 0% to 20%, AND its 20-session return in the top third of that evening's universe
definitions.weak: close below its own 50-day average, AND its 20-session return in the bottom third of that evening's universe
definitions.control: 50 symbols of that evening's universe, the lowest sha256('symbol|YYYY-MM-DD|SF1') first (fixed, not random at scoring time)
definitions.outcome: adjusted return from the next session's official open to the close 20 sessions later; no stop; costs left out because they are the same for every bucket (a delivery round trip is reported beside the result)
definitions.excess: bucket's equal-weight mean outcome minus the control's mean outcome, per recording evening

primary.statistic: D = mean over FALLING evenings of (strong excess - weak excess)
primary.prediction: D < 0 (in a falling market, strength does worse than weakness)

secondary.statistic: mean weak excess over RISING evenings
secondary.prediction: < 0 (laggards keep lagging in a rising market); reported, carries no verdict alone

descriptive.statistic: the managed book's actual replacement buys, tagged with the regime of their plan evening, and their +20-session excess over that evening's control

forward_review.recording: each evening after the managed book's run: one row per evening to paper/shadow/sf1/rows.jsonl holding the regime, the strong, weak and control member lists and their entry-day reference; each row carries the sha of the row before it and is refused on or after 09:15 IST of the next session, so it is a forecast, never hindsight
forward_review.scoring: nightly, any row whose 20 sessions have closed is scored once into paper/shadow/sf1/score.json; a scored row is never rewritten
forward_review.minimum: no verdict before 60 FALLING evenings spread over at least 3 separate falling spells of 10+ sessions; until then the state is INSUFFICIENT and the count of falling evenings and spells is shown
forward_review.expected_wait: falling evenings were about 21% of sessions in 2010-2017 and 48 of the last 120 sessions; the Nifty is above both averages today, so the primary may take many months to a few years. SF1-S and SF1-D accumulate meanwhile

bar.supported: D < 0 with a one-sided Newey-West t at or beyond 2.0 (19 lags for the overlapping 20-session windows) on the FALLING evenings, AND D < 0 inside at least two thirds of the separate falling spells. Then SF1-P is SUPPORTED_FORWARD
bar.rejected: D >= 0 once the minimum is reached: REJECTED_FORWARD, closed, kept on record
bar.otherwise: INCONCLUSIVE until the minimum is reached again with 30 more falling evenings, read once more, then closed whatever it shows

what_changes: nothing in any decision. SF1 is a shadow: no decision path imports it (a test proves it), no plan, cut, replacement, stop, rule, lock or the 60-session window is touched, and it is India only (no crypto data, never wakes the agent). If SF1-P is SUPPORTED_FORWARD, Claude writes one card proposing what the managed book's replacement ranking should do in a falling market; that card needs Madhav's own yes and then its own 20-session paper trial, like every rule
limits: one market regime definition fixed now, not tuned later
equal-weight buckets: a few names can move them, so the bucket sizes are printed with every score
cross-sectional terciles of 20-session return each evening (SP3 used training-year terciles); a fixed choice made now
the look that chose this hypothesis saw 2010-2017; forward rows from the first recording evening are the only evidence that counts
build_after_approval: india/sf1.py (record, score, show) beside india/managed.py; added to the evening and nightly jobs after the managed run; tests: the sha chain, the 09:15 IST refusal, a scored row never rewritten, no decision module imports sf1; one outside check of the build, then live
